subject: LuminaHealth demo follow-up — model roadtest, JSON ops, retry policy
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@luminahealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@luminahealth.com>

Subject: LuminaHealth demo follow-up — model roadtest, JSON ops, retry policy

Hi Aisha & Tom,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through the call summaries and a few representative transcripts. Quick recap and proposed next steps so the team can start a short roadtest: 

Key takeaways from our call:
- Primary use case: structured extraction from patient intake forms + callable actions to update EHR flags (severity, triage).
- Volume: ~15k requests/day initially, spiky during business hours (peaks ~200 reqs/min).
- Success criteria for roadtest: >= 95% schema-validated outputs on the provided prompt set; median token latency <= 220ms for the 75th percentile request shape.

Proposed roadtest plan (attached files: lumina_prompt_set_v1.yml, roadtest_eval_plan.csv):
1) Shortlist models to evaluate (see recommendations below). Goal: balance latency and deterministic schema compliance.
2) Run a 3-day run per model with the attached eval plan; we’ll collect structured-output pass rate, hallucination events, and token cost.
3) Tool-calling surface: we’ll simulate your EHR update call with a sandbox endpoint; test retry/backoff and idempotency behavior.
4) Deliverables: per-model perf sheet, a JSON-schema compliance report, and a recommended model+quantization profile.

Initial recommendations (high level):
- Narrow latency-focused: calliope-v2-8B-quant (good for lower-cost fp/int8 pipelines).
- Quality-focused variant: calliope-v1-3B-fp16 with stricter temperature and system prompt constraints.
- Fallback for complex utterances: flora-7b-int8 (higher recall on long context).

Schema & retry notes:
- We’ll validate structured output against your JSON schema on the service side and return a 422 with the validated error payload if a message fails validation.
- Recommend an exponential backoff with jitter for client retries (initial 100ms, max cap 1.6s, 3 retries) to avoid head-of-line amplification during spikes.

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Please confirm which subset of the prompt set you want in day-1 vs day-3 runs.
- Can procurement share PO / evaluation licensing constraints (Tom)?

I’m copying Camila and Marissa for technical setup and test harness details.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@luminahealth.com>

Subject: Re: LuminaHealth demo follow-up — model roadtest, JSON ops, retry policy

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock timelines: 

1) For schema validation, our compliance team insists on deterministic responses for certain fields (triage_level, consent_flag). If we detect >1% variance across runs we’ll need to fail the run. Which model/quant combo do you expect to be most deterministic?

2) Tool calling reliability: we need a guarantee that retrying the same tool call is idempotent from the model side (we handle dedupe on our endpoint). Does Redwood ship a recommended pattern for function-call output that makes dedup deterministic (e.g. explicit idempotency_token in the callable payload)?

3) Procurement: We can provide a template PO once you send an evaluation order form. Tom, can you confirm procurement cadence?

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll review the prompt set and flag day-1 examples.

— Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Clinical Product | LuminaHealth
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@luminahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: LuminaHealth demo follow-up — model roadtest, JSON ops, retry policy

Hi Aisha — short answers, then technical attachments and links below.

Determinism & model picks:
- Most deterministic: calliope-v1-3B-fp16 when constrained with deterministic sampling (temperature 0, top_p 1.0) and a tight system prompt. Expect >98% exact-field matches for short categorical fields (triage_level, consent_flag) on the prompt set you shared.
- Cost/latency tradeoff: calliope-v2-8B-quant is faster at inference and cheaper, but you’ll see slightly higher variance for long, multi-entity extraction. Expect ~93–96% exact-field matches on our sample set.

Function-calling / idempotency pattern:
- Recommendation: include an idempotency_token generated by the client and echoed in the model’s tool-call output. Redwood’s function response wrapper can validate that token and surface mismatches in the audit log.
- We also recommend explicit enum outputs where possible: e.g. {"triage_level":"LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH"} instead of free-text.

JSON schema validation and retries:
- Schema example attached (json_schema_example.json). Server behavior: on schema failure we return a 200 with a top-level field diagnostics.schema_pass=false and a debug.hint set; clients should treat that as a soft-failure and optionally reformat or re-run with an assistant-only prompt.
- Retry policy: client retry (3 attempts max) with exponential backoff and jitter, then escalate to the human-in-loop workflow if schema_pass=false after retries.

Benchmarks and infra links:
- Roadtest harness + sample dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDriveLink
- Preliminary microbenchmark report (calliope-v1 vs v2): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/lumina-health-report-2026

I attached the schema and the initial prompt set. I’ll provision a sandbox EHR endpoint and post the URL in the shared Drive folder by end of day.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
